ids_of_interest = {

}
# need full ids
cat = list(csv.DictReader(open(CATALOG_CSV)))
idmap = {}
for r in cat:
    key = r['point_uri'].split('#')[-1]
    idmap[key]=r['timeseries_id']
full = {
 'F3_Z01_temp': idmap['Zone_F3_Z01.Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor'],
 'F3_Z01_cool_sp': idmap['Zone_F3_Z01.Zone_Air_Cooling_Temperature_Setpoint'],
 'F3_Z01_heat_sp': idmap['Zone_F3_Z01.Zone_Air_Heating_Temperature_Setpoint'],
 'F2_Z01_temp': idmap['Zone_F2_Z01.Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor'],
 'F3_Z02_temp': idmap['Zone_F3_Z02.Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor'],
 'F3_Z03_temp': idmap['Zone_F3_Z03.Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor'],
 'F3_Z05_temp': idmap['Zone_F3_Z05.Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor'],
 'F4_Z01_temp': idmap['Zone_F4_Z01.Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor'],
}
data={}
for row in csv.DictReader(open(VALUES_CSV)):
    tid=row['timeseries_id']
    if tid in full.values():
        data.setdefault(tid,[]).append((row['timestamp'],float(row['value'])))
for k,v in full.items():
    ds=sorted(data.get(v,[]))
    print(k, len(ds), ds[0] if ds else None, ds[-1] if ds else None)

content.text: The data show a seasonal pattern: in warm months (summer) F3_Z01 tracks within ~0.5°C of the other zones, but in winter (Nov–Jan) it holds ~1.8–3.3°C above them while the others drop. All setpoints (cool 26.7 °C, heat 15.6 °C) are constant, so the setpoint didn't change. A constant sensor bias would shift all seasons equally; instead the excess appears when the heating/cooling demand is different (winter), which is consistent with an added local heat load in Zone_F3_Z01 that is masked when the cooling system works in summer.
